# BLO-40401: the DinD socket no longer mounts over the whole of `/var/run`

Files: `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`, `src/server/config-schema.ts`
(the last one is the operator-facing hint for `enableDocker`, which named the old socket path).

With `enableDocker: true` the builder mounted the shared `docker-sock` emptyDir at **`/var/run`** —
over the directory, not at `/var/run/docker.sock` — and appended that mount *after* the inherited
secret volumes. Anything the Deployment mounts beneath `/var/run` therefore vanished from the agent
container. The live one is `gbrain-authbot-service-key` at `/var/run/authbot`, so
`PAPERCLIP_GBRAIN_AUTHBOT_SERVICE_KEY_FILE` resolved into an empty tmpfs and the gbrain plugin's
OAuth-client read failed. Same silent-shadowing class as
[BLO-40279](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-40279): Kubernetes admits the Pod,
`kubectl describe pod` still lists the hidden mount, and only a read inside the container shows it
is gone.

Three changes:

1. The socket moves to a dedicated `/var/run/dind/docker.sock` (`DIND_SOCKET_DIR` /
   `DIND_SOCKET_PATH`, used by the sidecar's `--host`, both volumeMounts, `DOCKER_HOST`, and the
   wait preamble). It is now a *sibling* of `/var/run/authbot`, so neither can shadow the other.
   Not `/var/run/docker` — dockerd keeps its own runtime state there.
2. The per-container mount backstop, which previously caught only exact duplicates, now also
   rejects a mount declared as a strict **parent** of an earlier one. That is the shadowing shape;
   the reverse order (parent first, child after) is legal, visible, and stays allowed.
3. `initVolumeMounts` is reordered to match the main container's list. It led with `data`, i.e. the
   opposite order, so a nested `workspaceMountPath` was visible in `claude` and hidden in
   `write-prompt` — the init container's `mkdir -p ${dataMountPath}/...` then landed in the
   runtime-cache emptyDir and the main container never saw it. Found by (2); one order makes the
   shadowing verdict the same in both containers.

Not established, and deliberately not claimed: whether any agent currently runs with
`enableDocker: true`. It defaults to `false` and the only in-repo `true` is a test fixture, so this
may be latent — fixed anyway because the failure mode is silent.
